merkel_cell.label: Avelumab — metastatic Merkel-cell carcinoma · support plan
additional_support: Avelumab has minimal emetogenic risk in current NCCP. Premedication for the first four infusions prevents or reduces infusion reactions and is distinct from anti-sickness treatment. Confirm the medicine names and timing on the appointment plan. Other symptom treatments depend on the individual; immune-related symptoms need assessment rather than self-treatment alone.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests before every cycle. The nurse watches for infusion reactions and the team checks for bowel, breathing, skin, endocrine and other immune symptoms. Additional tests depend on symptoms, not just the routine blood panel.

Immunotherapy can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Contact the oncology team promptly for new or worsening diarrhoea, blood or mucus in stools, abdominal pain, cough or breathlessness, yellow skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, marked thirst, unusual weakness or a spreading rash. Tell every treating clinician that you are receiving or have received immunotherapy. During the infusion, tell the nurse immediately about chills, flushing, itching, chest or back pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty.

Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month after the last avelumab dose. Discuss fertility and breastfeeding with the team before treatment; do not substitute the different interval used for another immunotherapy.

This is the Merkel-cell cancer context after chemotherapy under current NCCP. It is not avelumab maintenance for urothelial cancer. Evidence from untreated first-line Merkel-cell cohorts must not be presented as the evidence for this specific post-chemotherapy indication.

melanoma.label: Melanoma · combination induction · up to four doses

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.timing: Day 1, if prescribed under the low-risk plan
medicines.note: Current NCIS V8 Table 1 p4. Review QT, electrolytes, constipation, hepatic dosing and interactions; this reference requires an individual prescription.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally up to three times daily as needed
medicines.timing: Subsequent days; duration to be prescribed
medicines.note: Review contraindications, renal function, interactions and extrapyramidal adverse effects.

additional_support: The medicine list is a source-based low-risk reference for an individual consultant-approved/local prescription; it is separate from infusion-reaction premedication and immune-toxicity steroid treatment.

NCCP classifies the combination phase as low emetogenic risk and nivolumab alone as minimal risk. Anti-sickness treatment is individual. Routine infusion premedication is not usually required; a previous reaction may alter that plan. Steroid or hormone treatment for immune effects must have a written follow-up plan.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests before every cycle, with symptom review during combination and maintenance phases. Cortisol and other organ tests are added when indicated. Recheck route, dose, interval and the maintenance start date when phases change.

Immunotherapy can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Contact the oncology team promptly for new or worsening diarrhoea, blood or mucus in stools, abdominal pain, cough or breathlessness, yellow skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, marked thirst, unusual weakness or a spreading rash. Tell every treating clinician that you are receiving or have received immunotherapy.

Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least five months after the final nivolumab dose. Discuss fertility and breastfeeding before starting and tell the team promptly if pregnancy is possible. Keep the last-dose date on the treatment record.

NCCP identifies nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg for melanoma as an unlicensed dosing posology in Ireland, despite reimbursement. Your clinician should explain this, the available alternatives and uncertainties, document informed consent under hospital policy, and follow the hospital Drug and Therapeutics Committee or equivalent acknowledgement process. CheckMate 511 primarily compared safety; it did not prove that this schedule has equal survival benefit to nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg.

melanoma.label: Melanoma · nivolumab maintenance
additional_support: Nivolumab maintenance has minimal emetogenic risk; no automatic low-risk induction antiemetic prescription carries over. Routine infusion premedication is not usually required; prior reactions and local policy govern individual support.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests before every cycle, with symptom review during combination and maintenance phases. Cortisol and other organ tests are added when indicated. Recheck route, dose, interval and the maintenance start date when phases change.

Your clinician should explain this, the available alternatives and uncertainties, document informed consent under hospital policy, and follow the hospital Drug and Therapeutics Committee or equivalent acknowledgement process. If a dose is delayed or held, obtain a revised written plan. The first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks after the last combination dose; the first four-weekly dose starts six weeks afterwards. Do not calculate a different start from the maintenance interval alone. Earlier immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions still apply.
